name: Slack
refreshNote: No official re-scrape tool. Slackbot-LinkExpanding responses are cached globally across Slack for around 30 minutes (api.slack.com/robots); after that, or with a changed URL (e.g. ?v=2), a new post re-fetches.
notes: Official (Slack Robots page): Slackbot-LinkExpanding fetches as little of the page as possible using HTTP Range headers and looks for oEmbed and Twitter Card / Open Graph tags; it also fetches referenced images/video/audio to check validity; responses cached ~30 minutes.

Slack developer blog: order is oEmbed first, then Twitter Card / Open Graph tags (whichever appears first in the HTML wins), then plain HTML meta tags. The fallback chain here (og before twitter) is a simplification - Slack actually prefers whichever tag comes first in the document.
twitter:label1/twitter:data1 and twitter:label2/twitter:data2 can add up to two extra label/value lines (not representable in this schema).
Layout: favicon + site name (og:site_name, else the host) on top, bold linked title, description, then image; grey left bar (theme-color not used, per available evidence).

Image: summary_large_image shows a large image; 'summary' shows a small square thumbnail at the right. Reports conflict on what happens without twitter:card - treat default as uncertain. Slack only honours the first twitter:card declaration. No documented size/byte limits (null); a ~60x60 minimum is a secondary-source claim. Some third-party sources say only the first ~32KB of HTML is read (unverified).
Truncation of title/description is not documented (null).

Verification method: official doc pages were located via web search (search-engine extracts of the official URLs listed in source); direct page fetches of the official domain were blocked from the research environment, so wording could not be re-read in full.
